newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hong Kong diesel very tight in post New Year buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong diesel very tight in post New Year buying.

text.p: Diesel stocks in Hong Kong, brimming just two months ago, have slid to very low levels after a price plunge triggered a Chinese buying spree after the Lunar New Year, trade sources in Hong Kong said on Thursday.
"Stocks are very low," one trader said. "Most of the tanks in Hong Kong are empty. Only one major oil firm has some cargoes, but not too much."
Traders said active sales into southern China from Hong Kong began when the price of diesel sold in barges started falling during the second half of February, after the Lunar New Year.
It hit a low of $203-$205 per tonne out of Hong Kong terminals, seen as very competitive compared with prices in China at 2,200 yuan (US$265) per tonne despite healthy supplies in inland China.
One Chinese trader said between mid-February and early March, about 100,000 tonnes of diesel moved from his Hong Kong terminal to southern China.
But traders noted that prices have risen again to about $220 per tonne from Hong Kong terminals.

Traders said prices on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to southern China had surged to around $215 per tonne, as values in Singapore have gained $2.25 a barrel over two weeks to $27.30 free-on-board (fob) basis.
They said the rally was largely due to a two-week buying spree by a Singapore trader who has already bought 2.32 million barrels of diesel for end March/early April lifting, fob basis.
The trader was believed to be in the market for more cargoes. Some sources said the trader was positioning himself for the Hong Kong and Chinese markets.

Traders also said China would need to buy diesel during its maintenance shutdown season, especially at the coastal refineries, starting in March. This could be one reason why supplies in Hong Kong have been snapped up, they said.
For example, the 150,000-barrel-per-day Dalian Petrochemical Co refinery had started a two-month rolling maintenance programme on its three crude distillation units on March 3.
But a source in Hong Kong with Sinochem, China's state trader, said the company would not rush to buy as long as prices remained at current high levels.
Sinochem would buy only when offers slip to $200-$202 per tonne, c-and-f southern China, he said. Another Hong Kong trader said a resonable level would be up to $205.

"There is a lack of supplies in the terminals, but they are waiting for the arbitrage cargoes from Russia and Europe to arrive in Asia during end March/early April to fill up the storage," the Sinochem source said.
About 500,000 tonnes of diesel has been fixed for delivery to Asia, where prices have outpaced those in the West. The price difference between the two regions reached $35 per tonne at one time.

Traders said buyers in Hong Kong and China were cautious at the moment as they wanted to avoid a similar situation when they bought huge volumes at record prices in December, resulting in a large build up in supplies in Hong Kong.
This caused prices to spiral downwards from early January, forcing many Chinese traders to lose money.
